evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Bare-clause merger question answered instead of counsel-flagged

cases.name: Pre-acquisition contract sweep
cases.query: We're negotiating to be acquired next year. Review the assignment and change-of-control provisions in this key customer contract from our side (the vendor being acquired).
files: contract: neither party may assign without consent (customer's consent in its sole discretion); 'any change of control of Vendor shall be deemed an assignment'; customer may terminate within 60 days of an unconsented assignment
baseline_risks: Summarizes 'mutual anti-assignment, standard'; the CoC-deemed-assignment + sole-discretion consent + termination right combo (a deal landmine) is not connected to the acquisition scenario
expected_behavior: Connects the clauses to the acquisition: the sale itself is a deemed assignment requiring the customer's sole-discretion consent
Maps the consequence: customer termination right within 60 days — a diligence/critical-path item
Preserves the sole-discretion consent standard; ranks this as the top issue
Counsel flag for structuring; negotiation direction (merger carve-out) noted
must_not: Miss the CoC-deemed-assignment landmine in the client's stated exit scenario

cases.name: Bare clause, merger question
cases.query: Our anti-assignment clause just says 'neither party may assign this Agreement without the other's consent' — nothing about change of control. If we're acquired in a stock sale, does that violate it?
baseline_risks: Answers the doctrine question directly ('stock sales are never assignments' or the reverse)
expected_behavior: Explains that whether a stock sale/merger triggers a bare anti-assignment clause depends on jurisdictional doctrine and transaction structure
Flags it for counsel rather than answering; notes what facts/structure details counsel will need
Suggests the drafting fix (express carve-out or express CoC language) for the future
must_not: Assert the doctrinal answer either way

cases.name: Rights-vs-duties coverage gap
cases.query: Review assignment provisions in this services agreement. We're the customer and care about who actually performs the work.
files: clause barring assignment of 'this Agreement' but silent on delegation/subcontracting of duties; vendor is quietly planning to subcontract performance
baseline_risks: Reports 'assignment is prohibited, you're protected' — missing that delegation/subcontracting of the actual work isn't covered
expected_behavior: Distinguishes assignment of the agreement from delegation of duties; finds the clause covers only the former
Flags that performance could be subcontracted without breach as written
must_not: Treat the bare anti-assignment clause as blocking subcontracted performance

cases.name: Asymmetry sold as mutual
cases.query: The counterparty says the assignment section is 'perfectly mutual — neither side can assign'. Sanity-check that for us before we sign.
files: clause: neither party may assign, EXCEPT that Party A may assign to any affiliate, successor, acquirer, or financing source without consent; Party B has no carve-outs; only Party B's change of control triggers Party A's termination right
baseline_risks: Confirms mutuality from the opening sentence
expected_behavior: Reads past the mutual-looking opener to the one-sided carve-outs and one-sided CoC trigger
Rejects the 'perfectly mutual' framing with citations
Recommends mirror carve-outs or removal as the ask

cases.name: Option acceleration question
cases.query: If we're acquired, does my stock option grant accelerate? Here's my grant agreement.
baseline_risks: Skill could analyze a commercial contract's CoC framework for an equity-acceleration question
expected_behavior: Recognizes an equity-acceleration question; routes to equity-incentive-review
must_not: Produce a commercial assignment analysis for an option-acceleration question
